claims.v: Fiscal Year 2023 Consolidated Annual Report on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena
claims.quote: Fiscal Year 2023 Consolidated Annual Report on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena
Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena CLEARED October 2023
For Open Publication Oct 17, 2023

claims.v: UNCLASSIFIED
claims.quote: UNCLASSIFIED Table of Contents

claims.v: United States
claims.quote: these reports mostly cover observations over U.S. airspace and littoral waters

claims.v: 31 August 2022 to 30 April 2023, plus earlier reports not included in an earlier report
claims.quote: The report covers unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) reports from 31 August 2022 to 30 April 2023, and all UAP reports from any previous time periods that were not included in an earlier report.

claims.v: NDAA for FY 2022, Section 1683(h), as amended by Section 6802(k) of the FY 2023 NDAA (50 U.S.C. § 3373)
claims.quote: in response to a requirement established in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022, Section 1683 (h), as amended by Section 6802(k) of the FY 2023 NDAA (as codified at 50 U.S.C. § 3373)

claims.v: due not later than 180 days after enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, then annually for four years
claims.quote: 180 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, and annually thereafter for four years

claims.v: a wide range of factors can influence observation and detection of UAP; observers convey their accurate recollection; sensors generally operate correctly
claims.quote: a wide range of factors can influence the observation and detection of UAP, observers convey their accurate recollection of their perception of the event, and that sensors generally operate correctly

claims.v: many reports are probably the result of sensor artifacts, equipment error, misidentification, or misperception
claims.quote: AARO and NIM-MIL recognize that many reports are probably the result of sensor artifacts, equipment error, misidentification, or misperception

claims.v: with better data most UAP will likely resolve to ordinary phenomena
claims.quote: the unidentified and purported anomalous nature of most UAP will likely resolve to ordinary phenomena and significantly reduce the amount of UAP case submissions

claims.v: the unidentified nature of most UAP is a consequence of gaps in domain awareness
claims.quote: continued volume and unidentified nature of most UAP is a direct consequence of gaps in domain awareness

claims.v: no UAP encounters confirmed to have contributed to adverse health effects
claims.quote: To date, no encounters with UAP have been confirmed to have directly contributed to adverse health-related effects to the observer(s).

claims.v: none of the UAP reports positively attributed to foreign activities
claims.quote: Although none of these UAP reports have been positively attributed to foreign activities, these cases continue to be investigated.

claims.v: space and maritime domains need to be fully integrated into AARO's processes
claims.quote: The space and maritime domains need to be fully integrated into AARO's processes.

claims.v: AARO and NIM-MIL strengthening targeted collection by the IC to mitigate collection bias
claims.quote: To further mitigate the inherent collection bias and to develop more comprehensive domain awareness, AARO and NIM-MIL are strengthening targeted collection by the IC.

claims.v: Appendix A: Case Closure Report, a pilot example of AARO's full-phase analytic process
claims.quote: Attached is a pilot example of the result of AARO's full-phase analytic process.

claims.v: Appendix B: Glossary of Terms
claims.quote: APPENDIX B: GLOSSARY OF TERMS

claims.v: Sources of anomalous detections in one or more domain (i.e., airborne, seaborne, spaceborne, and/or transmedium) that are not yet attributable to known actors and that demonstrate behaviors that are not readily understood by sensors or observers.
claims.quote: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomenon (UAP): Sources of anomalous detections in one or more domain (i.e., airborne, seaborne, spaceborne, and/or transmedium) that are not yet attributable to known actors and that demonstrate behaviors that are not readily understood by sensors or observers.

claims.v: Sources of anomalous detections above the Karman Line (i.e., 100 km above Earth's mean sea level).
claims.quote: Spaceborne UAP: Sources of anomalous detections above the Karman Line (i.e., 100 km above Earth's mean sea level).

claims.v: Sources of anomalous detections between Earth's mean sea level and the Karman Line.
claims.quote: Airborne UAP: Sources of anomalous detections between Earth's mean sea level and the Karman Line.

claims.v: Sources of anomalous detections at or below Earth's mean sea level within a body of water.
claims.quote: Seaborne UAP: Sources of anomalous detections at or below Earth's mean sea level within a body of water.

claims.v: Sources of anomalous detections that transit more than one domain.
claims.quote: Transmedium UAP: Sources of anomalous detections that transit more than one domain.

claims.v: Corporeal artifacts of UAP. UAP may contain one or more UAP objects (e.g., airborne craft exhibiting apparent anomalous capabilities). UAP material are samples, in whole or in part, of UAP objects (e.g., debris).
claims.quote: UAP Objects and Material: Corporeal artifacts of UAP. UAP may contain one or more UAP objects (e.g., airborne craft exhibiting apparent anomalous capabilities). UAP material are samples, in whole or in part, of UAP objects (e.g., debris).

claims.v: Any records of UAP detection, observation, identification, effects (on persons or equipment), mitigation, and material-exploitation.
claims.quote: UAP Data: Any records of UAP detection, observation, identification, effects (on persons or equipment), mitigation, and material-exploitation.

claims.v: Any occurrence where UAP is detected by persons or sensors.
claims.quote: UAP Incident: Any occurrence where UAP is detected by persons or sensors.

claims.v: Any UAP incident in, on, or near U.S. military installations, operating areas, training areas, special use airspace, proximity operations, and/or other national security areas of interest.
claims.quote: UAP Incursion: Any UAP incident in, on, or near U.S. military installations, operating areas, training areas, special use airspace, proximity operations, and/or other national security areas of interest.

claims.v: Bringing UAP under kinetic or non-kinetic fire, to deny, disrupt, or destroy the phenomenon and/or its object(s).
claims.quote: UAP Engagement: Bringing UAP under kinetic or non-kinetic fire, to deny, disrupt, or destroy the phenomenon and/or its object(s).

claims.v: The elicitation of UAP location, capabilities, characteristics, and/or intent using passive and/or active sensing capabilities
claims.quote: UAP Interrogation: The elicitation of UAP location, capabilities, characteristics, and/or intent using passive and/or active sensing capabilities

claims.v: The assessed natural or artificial source of the phenomenon and includes solar, weather, tidal events; U.S. Government, scientific, industry, and private activities; and foreign (allied or adversary) government, scientific, industry, and private activities.
claims.quote: UAP Attribution: The assessed natural or artificial source of the phenomenon and includes solar, weather, tidal events; U.S. Government, scientific, industry, and private activities; and foreign (allied or adversary) government, scientific, industry, and private activities.

claims.v: A safety hazard to persons, materiel, or information (e.g., from collision).
claims.quote: UAP Risk: A safety hazard to persons, materiel, or information (e.g., from collision).

claims.v: A force-protection and/or national- security threat to persons, materiel, or information by UAP that demonstrate hostile intent.
claims.quote: UAP Threat: A force-protection and/or national- security threat to persons, materiel, or information by UAP that demonstrate hostile intent.
This report was drafted by AARO and ODNI's National Intelligence Manager for Military Integration (NIM-MIL)
The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) received a total of 291 UAP reports during this period

claims.v: 801 as of 30 April 2023
claims.quote: as of 30 April 2023, AARO has received a total of 801 UAP reports

claims.v: de-conflicted cases with potential U.S. programs
claims.quote: AARO has de-conflicted these cases with potential U.S. programs and continues to work closely with its DoD and Intelligence Community (IC) mission partners to identify and attribute any objects found in these cases.

claims.v: new integrated analysis process assimilating raw intelligence into all-source data packages
claims.quote: AARO's new integrated analysis process ensures that raw intelligence related to UAP from various intelligence disciplines are assimilated into all-source data packages analyzed by teams of scientists and intelligence analysts.

claims.v: launched a public-facing website
claims.quote: AARO has launched a public-facing website that shares information about its mission, operations, UAP analytic trends and statistics, and declassified UAP data and footage.

claims.v: website to link to secure mechanism for authorized reporting of UAP
claims.quote: The website will also link to AARO's secure mechanism for authorized reporting of UAP.

claims.v: established classified collaboration mechanisms among government agencies
claims.quote: AARO has established classified collaboration mechanisms to encourage cooperation on UAP investigation and research among government agencies.

claims.v: declassified data and full-motion videos of UAP events for an open congressional hearing
claims.quote: AARO successfully exercised its process for declassifying data and full-motion videos of UAP events for an open congressional hearing held on 21 March 2023.

claims.v: sensor calibration campaign measuring known objects often reported as UAP
claims.quote: This plan includes a sensor calibration campaign to measure known objects that are often reported as UAP.

claims.v: developed models of known and unknown shapes for a simulator for sensor operators
claims.quote: AARO and its mission partners have developed models of known and unknown shapes that can be used within a simulator for sensor operators.

claims.v: physical testing, modeling and simulation, then peer review before reaching conclusions
claims.quote: This approach includes physical testing and employing modeling and simulation to validate analyses and the underlying theories, and then peer reviewing those results before reaching any conclusions.
A. Analytic Division AARO's analytic efforts are confirming
B. Operations and Collections Division During the period of reporting, AARO
C. Science and Technology Division In accordance with the FY 2022 NDAA
D. Strategic Communications Division AARO successfully exercised its process for declassifying

claims.v: only a very small percentage of UAP reports display interesting signatures
claims.quote: AARO's analytic efforts are confirming that only a very small percentage of UAP reports display interesting signatures, such as high-speed travel and unknown morphologies.

claims.v: normalized UAP operations, led development of reporting standards, informed acquisition of mission-specific sensors
claims.quote: further normalized UAP operations, led development of reporting standards; informed acquisition of mission-specific sensors; and guided integration of UAP detection, identification, and mitigation efforts

claims.v: established a multilayered science and technology plan
claims.quote: AARO has established a multilayered science and technology (S&T) plan that incorporates close partnerships with DoD Services, USG agencies, and other centers of excellence

claims.v: working to standardize and routinize the declassification process
claims.quote: AARO is working to standardize and routinize this declassification process to ensure as much transparency as possible.
